  • The class label and the episode definition agree on every cascade (Table 38). The two events whose largest overlapping episode falls below the $1m floor are 2025-04-03 10:01, at $84k and a forced share of 4.0%, and 2025-05-09 04:53, at $884k and 13.7%.
  • A surge containing a liquidation usually contains a small one. 57.8% of the no-big-price-move surges overlap an episode, and the median largest episode inside one liquidates $3.7k. Restricting to the $1m floor drops the share to 9.1%, so the 10% forced-share label separates the classes the way it is meant to.
  • Only 18 of the 47 cascades contain a whole episode. The other 29 overlap an episode that starts before the surge window or runs past its end, so the surge window and the liquidation run are not the same interval even where both fire.

Figure 8. HYPE liquidation episodes and flow-catalogue coverage, 15-minute gap rule.

What one mark is, and what the figure excludes

One mark per episode at the 15-minute gap rule, positioned at its first liquidation timestamp, with the summed liquidated notional on a logarithmic vertical axis. Every mark below the floor takes no part in the coverage statistic. The axis is clipped at $1k, which hides 1,056 of the 4,159 episodes; 93% of them liquidate one or two wallets and the largest holds 14. The band below the floor thins over 2025-04 to 2025-06 and again in 2026-03 and 2026-04, where a month holds 166 to 232 episodes against 300 to 381 in the busiest months.

Episodes above the floor arrive in every month of the window, and the misses sit at the bottom of the above-floor band throughout it, so the coverage gap follows episode size and holds in every period.

71.6 Findings

As expected.

  • The flow catalogues reach 62.1% of the above-floor episodes and 85.2% of their notional, clearing the decision rule's 60% bar, with 114 episodes standing outside both catalogues.
  • Coverage rises with the gap rule, 57.1% to 81.3% from 5 to 60 minutes, because a wider gap merges fragments into longer episodes that are more likely to touch a flow window.
  • The class label and the time episode agree at the top: all 47 one-sided surges labeled a liquidation cascade contain an episode, and 9 of the 10 largest episodes carry that label.
  • Long victims dominate 228 of the 301 above-floor episodes, and 9 of the 10 largest are forced sells, which matches a market whose liquidations cluster on down moves.

Not as expected (possible design cause).

  • The verdict flips with the gap rule. 57.1% at 5 minutes fails the 60% bar that 62.1% at 15 minutes passes. Possible design cause: the one-sided surge catalogue anchors on a 1-minute onset inside a 30-minute box and so selects short concentrated surges, while a 5-minute gap splits one liquidation run into fragments whose outer pieces fall outside that window. Check: recompute coverage with the episode interval padded by 5 and 10 minutes on each side, at every gap rule, and report how much of the 5-minute shortfall the padding recovers. This is decision D8 of section 64.11.
  • 75 of the 114 missed episodes stand more than 30 minutes from any flow event. The distance to the nearest one-sided surge or net-flow box reaches 962 minutes at p95 across the missed group. Possible design cause: these episodes liquidate a median $1.61m over 20.7 minutes, spread thinly enough that the minute-level taker flow never crosses the catalogues' entry bar. Check: read the 1-minute taker net and gross USD inside the 75 episode windows and compare them to the enter_bar_usd_1m of the surrounding 6 hours, then report how many sit below it.
  • The largest cascade is the least taker-driven. 2025-10-10 20:52 fills 77.9% of its $527.8m maker-side, against 97% to 100% taker for the other 9 in the top 10. Possible design cause: the forced share that defines the class label counts taker USD only, so the largest liquidation event in the sample contributes just $116.4m to it. Check: recompute forced_share on liquidated notional including maker-side fills and report how many additional one-sided surges cross the 10% bar. This is decision D7 of section 64.11.
  • 51 of the 561 quiet surges hold an episode above the $1m floor. That is 9.1% of the no-big-price-move class, against 25.5% of the big-price-move class. Possible design cause: the class label reads forced share against the window's total taker USD, so a $1m liquidation inside a heavy voluntary surge stays under 10%. Check: report the forced share of those 51 events and how many sit between 5% and 10%.

71.7 Validation

What was checked
  • Episode keys are unique. episode_id has 6,316, 4,159, 3,062 and 2,104 distinct values against the same row counts at the 5, 15, 30 and 60-minute gaps.
  • Episode notional reconciles to the stream at every gap. Summed episode notional is $1,965,151,446.77 at all four gap rules against $1,965,151,446.77 of qualifying liquidation notional, a difference of $0.000003, and summed trade counts are 101,590 at each.
  • Date-file boundaries are merged, not cut. The stream is concatenated and sorted on timestamp before the runs are formed, and 13, 19, 34 and 61 episodes span a UTC date boundary at the four gap rules. All 456 daily partitions were read and none was missing.
  • The distance to the nearest flow event was checked against a brute-force scan. Recomputing f1_gap_to_nearest_min for 400 randomly drawn episodes by comparing each against all 922 surge windows reproduces the stored value on all 400.
  • Every month in the window carries episodes. At the 15-minute gap each of the 15 calendar months holds between 166 and 381 episodes and between 2 and 40 above the floor; the busiest by notional is 2025-10 at $646.8m and the lightest 2025-04 at $14.6m. Per-month rows are in tables/casc0922_monthly.csv.
  • The named dates are present. 2025-10-10 holds 18 episodes, 2 above the floor, $536.2m, both overlapping a flow event; 2026-01-31 holds 17 episodes, 4 above the floor, $11.1m, 3 overlapping.

71.8 What this does not establish

  • An episode is HYPE only. A wallet liquidated in HYPE and in three other coins in the same minute appears once here, and a cross-margin cascade that shows in BTC and reaches HYPE late is dated by its HYPE trades.
  • ADL is excluded, so an unwind resolved by auto-deleveraging leaves no episode. The 6,230 ADL trades in the window carry $189.9m, 8.8% of the combined forced notional.
  • Episode notional is the grouped trade's notional. liquidated_volume equals volume on 99.76% of victim rows; on the remaining 0.24% the grouped order was only partly liquidated and this section counts the whole trade.
  • The fill table is incomplete from 2025-04-01 to 2025-05-25. Maker and taker HYPE do not balance on those dates, which affects the taker share and the flow catalogues' entry bars there. 2025-04 and 2025-05 hold 6 of the 301 above-floor episodes, so the coverage statistic barely depends on them.
  • Overlap is a timing test. An episode and a surge that share one minute count as overlapping, whichever caused the other, and this section makes no claim about direction.
  • The $1m floor is a level, not a percentile. It selects 301 episodes at the 15-minute gap and 82.7% of the liquidated notional; a floor at $500k or $2m would move the coverage share, and that sensitivity is not computed here.
